public_rationale: Zitron's claim is a judgment about what NVIDIA's financing deal signals. He calls it the 'loudest possible sign' that no one who can afford GPUs really wants them. In the same post he accepts that hyperscalers buy GPUs, but argues that demand traces back to OpenAI and Anthropic, who cannot pay from cash flow. So whether 'real demand' exists depends on how one treats that indirect demand, which is the point he is arguing. It is not a fact with an agreed measure. The announcement confirms only non-binding MOUs for financing platforms aimed at labs, enterprises and AI clouds. That neither proves nor disproves his reading.
limitations: Grading this would need a definition of 'real' or 'affordable' demand that the speaker did not give.
I did not read NVIDIA's own press release page; a trade outlet reproduced its text.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: NVIDIA's $500B private-credit financing arrangement shows there is no real GPU demand from buyers who can afford them.
